added: packages/deployment (@sos-2/deployment): the deployment contract — typed DeploymentRecords (Semantic Spine envelopes of the explicitly-registered add-only extension kind DeploymentRecord, the W3 ProvenanceRecord / W8 RecoveryDeclaration precedent) carrying deployment_id, environment, the EXACT artifact_revision (an ExactRevision CONSUMED from @sos-2/system-state, kind restricted to git-sha/config-version — deployment-id revisions identify deployments themselves and would be circular), a typed target_runtime ref (id + kind + version, structurally compatible with @sos-2/runtimes' RuntimeDescriptor), typed configuration values and the declared rollback; deterministic content-addressed ids; full validation (loud)

the declared rollback MIRRORS the recovery-control declarations by CONSUMING them: DeploymentRollbackDeclaration { mechanism, trigger, authority_ref, exception } — the mechanism/trigger validators (assertValidRecoveryMechanism/assertValidRecoveryTrigger), the GovernedException record and the boundedness POLICY (checkRecoveryDeclarationAgainstPolicy with require_bounded_recovery=true) are all @sos-2/recovery-control's own, so UNSPECIFIED-without-governed-exception is REJECTED exactly as W8 rejects it (no duplication, no weakening)

the deployment lifecycle PLANNED -> DEPLOYED -> ROLLED_BACK with VALIDATED transitions: carried by the envelope statuses (DRAFT -> ACTIVE -> RETIRED — a strictly narrower subset of the spine's legal transitions), so PLANNED -> ROLLED_BACK is FORBIDDEN here even though the spine would allow DRAFT -> RETIRED (you cannot roll back what was never deployed), ROLLED_BACK is terminal, re-deployment of a rolled-back deployment is rejected, identity is preserved across transitions (the spine discipline), and every transition is audited (caller-supplied RFC3339 instant + non-empty provenance in the store's transition log)

DeploymentOutcome records + the documented severity-lattice aggregation: outcomes carry the 6 frozen truth states verbatim; aggregateAvailability is the deterministic max-severity aggregation FAILURE > PARTIAL > UNKNOWN > UNAVAILABLE > UNSUPPORTED > SUCCESS (combining never increases apparent success — any UNKNOWN keeps the deployment UNKNOWN, a known FAILURE dominates, SUCCESS is the identity); summarizeDeploymentOutcomes reports ALL 6 keys zero-filled; DeploymentStore.statusOf reports a deployment with NO outcomes as UNAVAILABLE (a gap — never zero, never absence-of-failure); the store REFUSES simulated outcomes as real deployment status

the intervention-evidence bridge asInterventionEvidenceInput: deploying IS an intervention, so a REAL outcome mints an INTERVENTIONAL evidence input with VERBATIM availability (the W3 layer completes the minting); SIMULATED outcomes are refused loudly — never intervention evidence (the W9 simulator discipline)

the deterministic deployment SIMULATOR: simulateDeployment over declared scenario steps (success/unknown/unavailable probabilities) with a FIXED seed — the PRNG (mulberry32) is CONSUMED from @sos-2/experiments (no re-implementation, no ambient entropy, no hidden clocks), the stream is consumed in a FIXED order (three draws per step, always drawn, preserving alignment), and identical input yields BIT-IDENTICAL runs; every run is marked simulated (simulated: true + simulator version + exact seed in provenance) and simulatedRunOutcomes materializes inspection-only outcomes, all carrying simulated: true
preserved_invariants: failures preserve truth states (spec/architecture.md section 18 / R21, the W12 acceptance): outcome records and the aggregation never conflate UNKNOWN with UNAVAILABLE, SUCCESS or FAILURE — a deployment whose status is UNKNOWN is reported as EXACTLY UNKNOWN (pinned by tests through the spine's own assertTruthStateIs), and no-data is a gap (UNAVAILABLE) never read as zero or absence-of-failure (the architecture-lock forbidden shortcut)

live changes require bounded recovery (spec/architecture.md section 13): the deployment rollback declaration enforces the merged W8 policy VERBATIM through consumption — UNSPECIFIED mechanisms without an explicit governed exception are REJECTED (mechanism + trigger + authority are all mandatory, mirroring docs/assurance-model.md)

simulation is never intervention evidence (the W9 discipline): simulated deployment outcomes are refused by the store as real status and refused by asInterventionEvidenceInput loudly; every simulated run carries simulated: true, the simulator version and the exact seed in provenance (pinned by negative tests)

the Semantic Spine remains the ONLY identity/envelope/kind/serialization authority: DeploymentRecord is an explicitly-registered add-only extension kind; envelope creation and status transitions go through the spine's createEnvelope/withStatus; ids are content-addressed through the spine; exact revisions are the W2 contract consumed from @sos-2/system-state — no new core kind is touched, no envelope field changes, no second registry exists

every promoted change is reproducible from exact revisions (spec/architecture.md section 18 / R30): deployment records carry the exact artifact revision and the deterministic simulator is reproducible from the exact seed + declared steps

no frozen contract in spec/contracts/ was modified; spec/, docs/, root files and sibling-owned paths are untouched — all changes are additive under the owned path packages/deployment (the W12 owned-path contract)
boundary_changes: one new workspace package: @sos-2/deployment (runtime deps @sos-2/semantic-spine, @sos-2/provenance, @sos-2/system-state, @sos-2/recovery-control, @sos-2/experiments; dev-only dep @sos-2/evidence used by the intervention-evidence bridge tests) — one-directional and acyclic

the deployment lifecycle statuses (PLANNED/DEPLOYED/ROLLED_BACK) are a NEW typed domain vocabulary mapped onto the spine's frozen envelope statuses (a documented strict subset of legal transitions); the severity lattice over the frozen 6 truth states is a NEW documented aggregation order owned by this package — it never redefines any truth state, only combines them deterministically

the recovery-control declarations are CONSUMED (not structurally mirrored): W9 mirrored them only because W8 was unmerged at W9's base; W8 is merged at this base, so the consumption is exact (validators + policy + exception record from @sos-2/recovery-control)
